root_cause.text: The memcg refill_stock() function used get_random_u32_below() to select a victim slot for draining, but this function is not NMI-safe due to acquiring a per-CPU local_lock, and memcg charge draining can occur in NMI context, leading to potential corruption of the random subsystem’s per-CPU state.
root_cause.evidence: CVE description: "get_random_u32_below() is not safe to call in the nmi context and memcg charge draining can happen in nmi context... An NMI that lands on a CPU mid-update of the ChaCha batch state and recurses into the random subsystem would corrupt that state." Patch replaces the random pick with a per-CPU round-robin counter (drain_idx) guarded by the existing local_trylock.

intent_record.how: This introduces a per-CPU variable to track the draining index, which will be used to control the order or state of per-CPU memory cgroup stock draining at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace random stock slot selection with a lightweight round-robin policy to reduce overhead and simplify drain behavior.
intent_record.what: Replaced random index generation for stock draining with a sequential round-robin index using a new drain_idx field in the stock structure, including wrap-around logic.
intent_record.how: Instead of calling get_random_u32_below(NR_MEMCG_STOCK) to select a stock slot, the code now uses a monotonically increasing counter (stock->drain_idx) that wraps around modulo NR_MEMCG_STOCK, ensuring a deterministic and sequential selection of slots.
